texts.li: [tribal] {X_nameDef}, a gray-haired hunter of {FACTION}, has walked every trail between here and the sea, and says the one that led to this camp was the last. The pack {X_pronoun} dropped by the fire clanks like a cookpot.\n\nEverything in it is for sale, for {COUNT} silver, and most of it has been mended more than once.

[medieval] Forty years of other lords' wars, says {X_nameDef}, an old sellsword of {FACTION} on the road home. What {X_pronoun} wants now is a garden and a chair in the sun, and the kit would only rust there.\n\n{X_nameDef} unrolls it on the table piece by piece and asks {COUNT} silver for the lot.

[!lowtech] Thirty years a hired gun, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has a scar for most of them. {X_nameDef} showed a few at the gate without being asked.\n\nThe work is over, and the kit is for sale to anyone who'll keep it oiled. {X_nameDef} wants {COUNT} silver for the lot.
{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has more stories than teeth, and a pack of old gear to sell before {X_pronoun} settles somewhere for good. {COUNT} silver buys the lot.

li.label: Buy the gear ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts the silver and hands the gear over piece by piece, explaining where each dent came from.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay (may say no)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looks around the yard for a long moment, then sets the pack down by the door and asks which bed is {X_possessive}.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} turns the offer over through supper and says no, with thanks. There's a sister down south {X_pronoun} hasn't seen in twenty years. The stories go on late that night all the same.

li.label: An evening of stories
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} talks until late, mostly about bad roads and the one time {X_pronoun} nearly got rich. Nothing from the pack changes hands.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shoulders the pack, grunts at the weight of it, and goes on down the road.

texts.li: [lowtech] A measuring chain forty paces long rattled out of {X_nameDef}'s satchel when {X_pronoun} set it on the table. {X_nameDef} makes maps for {FACTION}, and would make one of the colony's land too: every slope and cliff, and whatever shows in the rock.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver it would be done properly. With {A_nameDef} along to show the way, {X_nameDef} would go over the land for nothing, faster and rougher, and promise nothing.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has a theodolite strapped to {X_possessive} pack and a tablet full of contour lines, and the colony's hills aren't on it yet. A proper survey would cost {COUNT} silver, and {X_nameDef} says there's always ore somewhere in hills like these.\n\nIf {A_nameDef} comes along to save time, the survey is free. It will also be rough, and might find nothing.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} draws maps for a living, and has asked to draw the colony's. For {COUNT} silver the survey will be thorough. With {A_nameDef} as a guide it costs nothing, and may come to nothing.

li.label: Pay for a survey ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the silver and goes up into the hills. The map {X_pronoun} leaves the colony is a single sheet, with one place circled twice.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} guide {X_objective} (may find nothing)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes up into the hills with {X_nameDef}, holding the far end of the line and asking questions. The survey is rough, and it cost nothing.
li.riskOutcome: Every face of rock {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} look at is plain and gray. There's nothing worth digging, though {A_nameDef} comes back able to read a map properly.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} folds up the charts and moves on to the next valley.

done.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef}'s survey found a seam of {THING} in the rock {PLACE}, close enough to the surface to dig out. It's marked with a cairn and a strip of red cloth.
[!lowtech] The survey turned up a seam of {THING} in the rock {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} marked it on the colony's map and sprayed an orange cross on the rock face before leaving.
{X_nameDef} put {A_nameDef}'s hand flat on the rock {PLACE} and said to dig there. Under the weathered face is a seam of {THING}.

titles.li: [medieval] A monk of a silent order

texts.li: [tribal] A spirit-walker of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, has come to the camp with ash on {X_possessive} face. {X_nameDef} is keeping a season of silence, and asks with {X_possessive} hands for a place to sit near people for a day or two.\n\n{A_nameDef} has had a hard time of late, and has been watching the spirit-walker since {X_pronoun} came.

[medieval] {X_nameDef}, a monk of a silent order from {FACTION}'s lands, came to the gate with a slate and a stub of chalk. On the slate, in careful letters: "A place to sit, near people. A day or two. Then I go."\n\n{A_nameDef}, who hasn't been sleeping well, keeps finding reasons to pass the gate.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} stood at the gate with folded hands for an hour before anyone thought to bring paper and a pencil. {X_nameDef} wrote four words and handed them back: sit near people, please.\n\nIt was {A_nameDef} who brought the paper. {A_nameDef} has been having a bad time, and hasn't gone far from the gate since.

[troubled] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} speaks with {X_possessive} hands and nothing else: a place to sit, near people, for a day or two. {A_nameDef}, who has had a bad few days, hasn't taken {A_possessive} eyes off the stranger.

li.label: Let {X_objective} stay
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} settles by the fields with folded hands. People find themselves going over to sit nearby for a while, and coming back calmer.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to sit with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} sit side by side for hours without a word between them. {A_nameDef} comes away with {A_possessive} shoulders down, and yawning.

li.label: Send {X_objective} on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} bows and walks on down the road.

done.li: [sat] {TALE} has gone on without a sound, the way {TALE} came. The silent guest left a parting gift, {ITEM}, and it was {A_nameDef} who found it.
[stayed] The silent guest has left the way {TALE} arrived, without a word to anyone. Left behind for the colony there is {ITEM}.
{TALE} has gone. The only sign the silent guest was ever here is {ITEM}, set down neatly for the colony to find.

texts.li: [leg] A cart came into the yard with legs hanging from its frame like hams in a smokehouse, in every size. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} makes them, and took one look at {A_nameDef} crossing the yard before offering a {TALE}, measured and fitted before {X_pronoun} leaves.\n\n{COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} says, or {PLACE} in materials.

[foot] {X_nameDef}, a limb-maker of {FACTION}, watched {A_nameDef} limp across the yard and already has the measurements in {X_possessive} head. A {TALE} could be carved and fitted before supper.\n\nIt costs {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials.

[arm] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has fitted a few hundred arms in {X_possessive} time, and remembers most of the people wearing them. {X_nameDef} would like to fit {A_nameDef} with a {TALE} before moving on.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials if the colony would rather.

[jaw] For {COUNT} silver, or {PLACE} in materials, {X_nameDef}, a maker of false parts from {FACTION}, will fit {A_nameDef} with a {TALE} while {X_pronoun} waits. {A_nameDef} hasn't eaten anything chewier than porridge in a long time.
{X_nameDef}, a limb-maker of {FACTION}, is passing through and has offered {A_nameDef} a {TALE}, for {COUNT} silver or {PLACE} in materials.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} measures, carves and fits, and {A_nameDef} has a {TALE}.

li.label: Pay in materials ({PLACE})
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sorts through the materials, takes what {X_pronoun} needs and gets to work, and {A_nameDef} has a {TALE}.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} packs up the cart and moves on.

li.label: Pay a little to have {X_objective} teach our best crafter
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shows {B_nameDef} how a {TALE} is measured and shaped, and lets {B_objective} make the cuts. {A_nameDef} still goes without, but the measurements are in {B_nameDef}'s notebook now.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {X_nameDef} sits {B_nameDef} down with a block of ash and shows {B_objective} how a {TALE} is carved, joint by joint. The offcuts are all over the workshop floor, and {A_nameDef} will have to wait for {B_nameDef} to make the real one.
[leg] {X_nameDef} fits and pads the new {TALE}, and {A_nameDef} walks the length of the colony on it, slowly at first, then again, faster.
[foot] {X_nameDef} fits the {TALE}, and {A_nameDef} walks back and forth across the yard on it, trying it on every kind of ground.
[arm] {X_nameDef} fits the new {TALE}, and {A_nameDef} picks up a cup with it, then every other cup in the kitchen to be sure.
[jaw] {X_nameDef} fits the {TALE}. At supper {A_nameDef} means to eat the toughest piece of meat in the pot, slowly and with great satisfaction.

texts.li: "Salt," said {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, before even sitting down. "On the coast they all but give it away, and inland they'll pay anything for it." A caravan leaves soon, and {X_nameDef} wants backers: twice the stake back in about ten days.\n\n{A_nameDef} heard the whole pitch out without a word. Caravans get lost, and not every merchant is one.

[trader] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knew {A_nameDef} in the trading days, and greeted {A_objective} at the gate like a cousin. Now {X_nameDef} is putting a caravan together and wants the colony in on it, for twice the stake back in about ten days.\n\n{A_nameDef} says {X_nameDef} paid {X_possessive} debts back then, though not always on the day.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} wants backers for a trade run, and has the terms written on a card.

Two trucks, one run across the wastes.
Back in about ten days.
Twice the stake to every backer.

{A_nameDef} has read the card three times and is now reading {X_nameDef}.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a merchant of {FACTION}, is buying a string of pack mules for a run to the river towns with wool, and needs backers. {X_nameDef} offers twice the stake back in about ten days, sealed with a handshake and a scratched receipt.\n\n{A_nameDef} went out to look at the mules, and they're real. What the rest is worth, {A_nameDef} can't say.

li.label: Put in {COUNT} silver (it may not come back)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counts the silver twice and writes a receipt for {A_nameDef} on the back of an old bill of sale. The caravan should be home in about ten days.

li.label: Put in {TALE} silver (it may not come back)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} had hoped for more and says so, then writes the receipt anyway and shakes {A_nameDef}'s hand. About ten days, {X_nameDef} says on the way out.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs and goes to try the next settlement down the road.

extra.li: The colony has {ITEM} silver in its stores.

coming.li: {TALE}'s caravan venture, with {COUNT} of the colony's silver in it, is due back in about {DAYS}.

done.li: [good] Every pack on {TALE}'s caravan came home empty, the way a merchant likes them. {TALE} has sent the colony its share: {COUNT} silver, about twice what went in.
[good,lowtech] {COUNT} silver in a knotted sack has come from {FACTION}'s lands, the colony's share of {TALE}'s venture. Tied to the knot is a strip of bark with three words cut into it: sold it all.
[lost] A storm caught {TALE}'s caravan in the passes and sent half the goods down the mountainside. What {TALE} could save of the colony's stake has come back with an apology, {COUNT} silver of it.

[lost] Bandits stopped {TALE}'s caravan in its second week on the road and kept most of it. {TALE} got away with the strongbox, or what was left in it, and has sent the colony {COUNT} silver, its share of very little.

fail.li: {TALE}'s caravan is days overdue, and {FACTION}'s people have never heard of {TALE}, or of any caravan at all. The colony's silver is gone.
The receipt {TALE} wrote out has turned out to be worth exactly the paper it's on. There was never any caravan, and there won't be any silver.

texts.li: {FACTION} want the colony's prisoner, {X_nameDef} of {ENEMY}, and have sent riders to say so. {X_nameDef} raided one of their villages last year, they say. They'll pay {COUNT} silver and take {X_objective} back to stand trial.\n\nThey don't say what kind of trial.

[lowtech] "That one burned a farm of ours and killed the herdsman," said the rider from {FACTION} at the gate, loud enough for {X_nameDef} of {ENEMY} to hear it in the cells.\n\n{FACTION} will pay {COUNT} silver to have {X_objective} handed over. {X_nameDef} has gone very quiet.

[!lowtech] {FACTION} have sent their offer over the comms, in the clipped way of people who give orders for a living.

Prisoner: {X_nameDef}, of {ENEMY}.
Wanted: one year, for raiding.
Offered: {COUNT} silver on transfer.
Collection: today.

The message ends there.

li.label: Hand {X_objective} over ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes with {FACTION}'s riders in irons, and doesn't look back at the colony. Their silver stays behind.

li.label: Release {X_objective} instead
li.outcome: The wardens are told to let {X_nameDef} go. {FACTION}'s people leave without another word.

li.label: Keep {X_objective} here
li.outcome: The colony keeps its prisoner. {FACTION}'s riders leave the way they came, with their silver and a grudge.

remembered.li: {ENEMY} haven't forgotten that the colony sold {TALE} to {FACTION}.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} followed a trail of blood into the brush beyond the fields and found {X_nameDef} at the end of it, half-conscious, with a bad wound and a weapon {X_pronoun} won't let go of. {X_nameDef} won't say who did it or why. A place to lie low is all {X_pronoun} asks for.\n\nSomeone did this on purpose, and may want to finish it.

[winter] Out on the land, {A_nameDef} found tracks in the snow, then blood, then {X_nameDef}, curled up under a ledge and shaking. {X_nameDef} is hurt and armed, and won't say how {X_pronoun} got hurt.\n\nLeft out there tonight, {X_nameDef} may not see morning.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} came back from the woods at a run. A stranger, {X_nameDef}, is lying hurt in a hollow by the stream, with a blade in {X_possessive} fist that {X_pronoun} won't put down.\n\n"Who did this?" {A_nameDef} asked. "Better you don't know," said {X_nameDef}.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} found {X_nameDef} slumped against a rock beyond the fields, a field dressing soaked through and a rifle across {X_possessive} knees. The barrel was still warm.\n\n{X_nameDef} asks for a place to lie low, and answers no questions.

li.label: Bring {X_objective} in (someone may come looking)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is carried in and put to bed. As soon as {X_pronoun} can stand, {X_nameDef} says, {X_pronoun} will earn {X_possessive} place.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} is carried in and put to bed. Back where {X_pronoun} lay there are fresh tracks, several sets of them: {ENEMY}, looking. They'll come for {X_nameDef} within days.

li.label: {ENEMY} want {X_nameDef}
li.text: {ENEMY} have tracked {X_nameDef} to the colony, and they've come to finish what they started.

li.label: Leave food and bandages (may be repaid)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sets bread and clean bandages within {X_nameDef}'s reach and comes home. What happens now is up to the stranger.

li.label: Leave {X_objective} there
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks away, and doesn't go back to look.

done.li: [lowtech] A bundle has turned up for the colony, wrapped in oilcloth and tied with a strip of old bandage. Inside is {ITEM}, and a piece of bark with one name cut into it: {TALE}.
[!lowtech] The watch found a bundle left for the colony, tied with a length of old bandage. In it was {ITEM}, and a scrap of paper. "For the bread. {TALE}."
Whoever left the bundle didn't stay to be thanked. It holds {ITEM}, and it's tied with one of the colony's own bandages, the kind that was left for {TALE}.

titles.li: [medieval] A herald under a white flag

texts.li: [tribal] A pipe-bearer of {ENEMY} has come alone and sat down in the grass beyond the fields with a carved pipe across {X_possessive} knees. {X_nameDef} has come to talk of ending the feud.\n\nThe price of peace is {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}. The pipe stays unlit until it's paid.

[medieval] A herald of {ENEMY} waits on the road below the colony under a white flag, and recites the offer to anyone who will come down to hear it.

"For {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} from your stores, {ENEMY} will put up their swords, and the blood between us is paid in full."

The herald, {X_nameDef}, has said it four times now, word for word.

[!lowtech] {ENEMY} have sent an envoy, {X_nameDef}, who waits outside the colony under a white flag with empty hands held where the colony's guards can see them. The offer is short: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}, and the fighting stops.
{ENEMY} are tired of the feud. So says {X_nameDef}, who walked up the road unarmed to say it, and named the price of peace: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE}.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver for peace
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} takes the silver back to {ENEMY}, and their answer comes the same day. The feud is over.

li.label: Pay {TALE} for peace
li.outcome: The food goes out to the envoy sack by sack, until the envoy nods. {ENEMY} will send their own people to haul it home, and the feud is over.

li.label: Send the envoy away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back to {ENEMY} with nothing to show for the walk. The feud goes on.

remembered.li: {FACTION} have kept the peace since their envoy came.
The peace with {FACTION} was bought, and so far it's holding.

texts.li: [their:grudge] The tithe {FACTION} want this year has grown, and {X_nameDef}, their lord's reeve, doesn't pretend otherwise. There is bad blood between {FACTION} and the colony, and it has found its way into the ledger: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} in kind, to be carried to {PLACE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} doubts the colony's land was ever in anyone's ledger, and would like to say so.

{X_nameDef}, reeve to a lord of {FACTION}, unrolled the claim at the gate and read it out.

"The fields below the hill lie within my lord's lands, and my lord's lands owe their tithe. Let {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} in kind, be carried to {PLACE} before the month is out."

{A_nameDef} asked whose seal was on the deed. The reeve's answer was long, and didn't name one.

[fall] The harvest is in, and so is {X_nameDef}, reeve to a lord of {FACTION}, come to collect the tithe on it. The colony owes {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} says, or {TALE} from its stores, for land the lord's grandfather once rode across.\n\n{A_nameDef} would very much like to see the deed.

{X_nameDef} wears the badge of a lord of {FACTION} and has come to collect a tithe for {PLACE}: {COUNT} silver, or {TALE} in kind. The colony has never paid anyone a tithe.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks it shouldn't start now, and is ready to argue the point.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} weighs the silver, writes the colony into the ledger and rides off.

li.label: Pay in kind ({TALE})
li.outcome: The sacks are counted, every one of them entered in the ledger, and set aside for the lord's carters.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} dispute it (losing costs more)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} argues the boundaries stone by stone until {X_nameDef} gives up and shuts the ledger. The lord, {X_nameDef} says, will look into it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} argues, but {X_nameDef} has the deed, the seal and all afternoon. The colony pays the tithe, and a fine on top for wasting the reeve's time.

li.label: Refuse
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes something long in the ledger, underlines it twice and rides off without another word.

texts.li: [!lowtech] A survey drone with {FACTION}'s markings came down {PLACE} trailing smoke, and split its casing open where it hit.\n\n{A_nameDef} thinks there's still something in its memory, maps or scans, maybe more. {FACTION} will want it back, and would likely pay for it.

[spacer] A {FACTION} scout drone dropped out of the sky {PLACE} with a dead thruster and buried its nose in the dirt. Its core is still blinking.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants a try at the data before the core wipes itself. Stripped, it's a handful of parts, and its owners would pay a reward to have it back whole.

[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} heard a whine and a crunch {PLACE}, and found a drone of {FACTION}'s nose-down in a furrow of torn earth, one rotor still turning.\n\nIts memory might hold something worth having, if {A_nameDef} can get into it before it wipes. Otherwise there are the parts, or {FACTION}'s reward for its return.

li.label: Strip it for parts
li.outcome: The drone comes apart bolt by bolt into components and good steel. The scorched lump of casing is left where it fell.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} pull its memory (it may wipe itself)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} gets into the memory before it can wipe, and copies out reams of survey data. Some of it bears on what the colony is researching, and a couple of components come out of the casing besides.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} gets the casing open, but the core wipes itself the moment {A_pronoun} touches it. One component is all that's left worth having.

li.label: Return it to {FACTION} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {FACTION} send someone to collect the wreck, with {COUNT} silver and their thanks.

texts.li: [!lowtech] The comms have been repeating the same transmission every hour since it started: a call sign, eleven numbers, and four seconds of silence before it begins again. {A_nameDef} has written the numbers down. They never change.\n\nAnswering would tell whoever is listening where the colony is. {A_nameDef} could try to trace it and keep the colony's own set silent.

[spacer] A looped call for help is coming through on the comms in an old spacer code, weak and patient. It could be a survivor. It could be a beacon that has outlived its ship, or bait.\n\n{A_nameDef} can try to trace it without answering, or the colony can answer it.

[!lowtech] Three words, over and over, on a frequency nobody has used in years. {A_nameDef} has been listening at the comms since breakfast and still isn't sure what the words are. The voice sounds tired.\n\nThe colony could answer. {A_nameDef} could also try to find where it's coming from without giving the colony away.

li.label: Answer it (it may be a lure)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} answers the signal.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} answers, and the signal cuts off mid-word. An hour later another channel lights up with laughter and the colony's own coordinates read back. {ENEMY} are coming.

li.label: {ENEMY} answer back
li.text: The signal was bait. {ENEMY} traced the colony's answer, and have come to see what they caught.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} trace it without answering
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} narrows the signal down to a spot out on the colony's own land.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} chases the signal across three bands until it fades into static and doesn't come back.

li.label: Leave it
li.outcome: The signal is left to repeat itself, and before long it stops.

outcomes.li: [survivor] {A_nameDef} answers, and a hoarse voice comes back: {X_nameDef}, alone in a damaged escape pod for days. {A_nameDef} talks {X_objective} down toward the colony, and the pod is coming in now.

[survivor] {A_nameDef} answers, and after a long silence a voice says thank you, three times. It's {X_nameDef}, the last one left on a drifting wreck, with one pod still working. The pod is on its way down.
[beacon] {A_nameDef} answers. Nothing answers back. It's an automated beacon, still calling from a wreck that was picked clean years ago.
[beacon] {A_nameDef} answers, and gets an automated reply: the same call sign, the same numbers. Whoever set the beacon running is long gone.

done.li: The signal came from an old transmitter half buried {PLACE}, wired to a battery that should have died years ago and to a cache of supplies. {A_nameDef} dug the cache out: {ITEM}.
{A_nameDef} followed the signal to a rusted beacon half sunk in the ground {PLACE}. Beside it, under a tarp gone stiff with age, was what someone meant to come back for: {ITEM}.

texts.li: [gifted] {X_nameDef}, a wandering scholar of {FACTION}, keeps one book wrapped in oilcloth at the bottom of {X_possessive} pack: {THING}. It's the real thing, {X_nameDef} swears, and it opens only to someone with the gift.\n\n{A_nameDef} has the gift, and hasn't been able to look away from the book since it came out of the pack. {X_nameDef} asks {COUNT} silver.

[ungifted] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} sells old books off the back of a mule, and one of them is the real thing: {THING}. Nobody in the colony has the gift to use it yet, {X_nameDef} admits, but books like this are rare, and the right person may come along.\n\nThe price is {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Buy it ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} unwraps the book, lets {A_nameDef} hold it for a moment and takes the silver.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} wraps the book up again, slowly, and moves on.
